key_insight: A quantum convolutional neural network can act as a surrogate model for predicting groundwater heat plume behavior, with competitive performance that improves when error mitigation is applied on real quantum hardware.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a path toward reduced-order, quantum-assisted forecasting for geothermal groundwater systems where full physics simulations are too expensive for routine use.
method: Encode reduced groundwater temperature targets using a Hamiltonian-inspired feature map.
Apply a QCNN with quantum convolution, quantum pooling, and a quantum readout stage.
Test across statevector, noisy simulation, IBM Kyiv hardware, and error-mitigated hardware.
evidence_signal: Performance was evaluated with mean squared error on training and testing sets, showing the QCNN was competitive on simulators and improved under mitigation, though classical networks remained best overall.
watch_item: The surrogate relies on heavy dimensionality reduction and current quantum hardware noise, so practical accuracy may depend strongly on target compression and mitigation quality.
paper_title: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks for Groundwater Heat Plume Prediction: A Surrogate Modeling Approach
